DATE: TIME: REPUBLIC OF THE PHILIPPINES DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNM A. Francisco Gold Condominium II EDSA Cor. Mapagmahal St., Diliman Quezon City LEGAL SERVICE NA PALAXAD. DIR. FRANCISCO C. JOSE, CESO IV Regional Director DILG-Region X1 DILG Legal Opinion No. 92 s. 2011 DEC 05 2011- 58 Mac Arthur Highway, Matina, Davao City Dear Dir. Jose: This has reference to your 09 November 2011 Memorandum requesting the Central Office's opinion on whether DILG-DBM, JMC No. 2011-1 applies to barangays created by the city or provincial government. The query sprung from the letter of Barangay Vicente Hizon, Sr., Davao City Punong Barangay Ralph O. Abella requesting from Davao City Accountant Rizalina Justol the exemption of his barangay from the mandatory allocation of at least 20% in the Annual Barangay Budget for the Barangay Development Fund. PB Abella opines that since Barangay Hizon is created by the City Government of Davao and is only receiving a City Aid in lieu of Internal Revenue Allotment, his barangay is not required to comply with the mandatory budgetary allocation for development programs. Furthermore, the "City Aid" was taken from the City Budget net of the 20% deduction of the City Development Fund. Your Region opines that while technically, the term "Internal Revenue Allotment" refers to the share of local government in the national budget to be released by the DBM, the City Aid should be treated akin to IRA allocation which was spliced from the City Government Budget. This being so, the Annual Budget of Barangay Hizon should be subject to the same conditions, including the 20% allocation for the development projects, as mandated by the Local Government Code of 1991. Based on the foregoing premises, we concur with your opinion. The "financial aid" given by City of Provincial government which created the barangays should be treated akin to an IRA allocation. In DILG Opinion No. 34, s. 2004, we had the occasion to interpret Section 285 of the Local Government Code of 1991, viz. : "May we point out that under Section 285 (last par.) of the Local Government Code of 1991, it is so provided that: "Provided, finally, that the fiscal requirements of barangays created by LGUs after the effectivity of the Code shall be the responsibility of the local qovemment units concerned." (Underlining ours). In relation thereto, Article XIV (g) of the Implementing Rules and Regulations of RA 7160 provides: "(g) Financial requirement - the financial requirements of the barangays created by LGUs after the effectivity of the Code shall be the responsibilitv of the LGU concerned." (Underlining ours). In that regard, may it be noted that barangays may be created through a law enacted by Congress or through an ordinance by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan with respect to the creation of new barangays in a municipality, or by the Sangguniang Panlungsod, with respect to the creation of new barangays within a city (Secs. 385 and 386, RA 7160). The aforequoted provisions expressly provides that the financial requirement of the barangays created created by LGU, i.e., by the provincial

Code, shall be the responsibility of the LGU concerned. Corollarily, the phrase "local government units concerned" undoubtedly refers to the local government units which created the new barangays and obviously that refers also to the provincial or city government, as the case may be. Accordingly, with respect to the financial requirement of the newly created barangays in your municipality, their IRA share should be borne by the provincial government, being the creating LGIJ " Obviously, Section 285 of the Code intended the "financial aid" granted to barangays created by the city or provincial government to be treated in the same manner as the IRA. This means that 20% of this "financial aid" should be allotted by the barangays for Development Projects which shall be subject to application of rules and regulations issued by this Department and the DBM with regard to its utilization. In the case of Barangay Hizon, since the PhP 1.8 M "City Aid" granted by the City of Davao was taken from the 20% City Development Fund, the utilization of the entire amount should be subject to the rules and regulations issued by the Department and the DBM, i.e., DILG DBM JMC No. 2011-1 and other similar issuances, since it remains to be part and parcel of the 20% development fund. We hope the foregoing sufficiently addresses your concern. Very truly yours, JESUS Di rect .D 111
